note: The library and family archive of the De Franceschi of Gologorica survive. They are in the National and University Library in Zagreb, they have been catalogued, and until September 2026 this project did not know they existed.
lead: Carlo De Franceschi told Kobler in 1876 that his great-great-grandfather built the family's house at Gologorica in 1711. What was inside that house — the books, the correspondence, the drafts of Carlo's own histories, the estate papers, the photographs — was not destroyed in 1945. It was carried to Zagreb, put in boxes, and left there for more than fifty years. It is now on a catalogue, under a shelfmark of its own, and anyone can ask for it.

rows.l: the span of the printed collection
rows.w: A Machiavelli of 1550, a Cipolla of 1555, Naldini's description of Capodistria of 1700, Tanara's household economy of 1680, Bembo's letters of 1743, an Ovid of 1753, Bonomo on the ancient counts of Gorizia of 1785

rows.l: and seven folders — the family archive
rows.w: 39 × 29 × 23.5 cm each, with a summary description of every box
«Poklon De Franceschi» — the De Franceschi Gift. Records run from PDF 0.001 to beyond PDF 0.745

archive.heading: And the archive is the part that matters
archive.text: After the books were done the family archive itself was arranged. What is in the fourteen boxes, in the paper's own words: manuscript drafts of the scholarly and specialist works of Carlo senior and of Camillo; family correspondence; personal and estate documentation; photographs and one photograph album; and pencil drawings on paper by the painter Giulio De Franceschi.
archive.why: Every one of those categories bears directly on this archive. The drafts are the working papers behind «L'Istria: note storiche». The family correspondence is the other half of the letters to Kobler. The estate documentation is the paper trail of the household that farmed the bishop of Pedena's rent. And there is a photograph album from a house this project has never seen a picture of.

steps.w: «Gologorica near Pazin, which was the centre of the political and cultural life of that district. In the house were a rich library and the family archive.»
After the capitulation of Italy the family went to Italy.

«Njihova je tiskana i rukopisna građa 1945. pronađena izbačena iz ormara i razbacana po kući» — their printed and manuscript material was found in 1945 thrown out of the cupboards and scattered about the house.
Most of it reached the National and University Library, where it stood for more than fifty years unprocessed and inaccessible, in the depots of the old building and then the new.
The first bibliographic record was entered on 15 May 2009. A second phase ran through 2014. Work on the last material to be found began on 20 January 2021.

marks.heading: They had no bookplate. They signed their names.
marks.text: Of 2,341 books, only 217 carry any mark of ownership at all — just over nine per cent. And the De Franceschi never had an ex libris of their own: they wrote their names instead, usually on the title page, often with a date and very seldom with a place.

names.w: The commonest, and ambiguous: it can be Carlo or Camillo, at least in books published before Carlo died in 1893.
Appearing as G. P. De Franceschi, G. Pietro, and G. P. de Franceschi.
One book. The only woman of the family to have signed one.
Signed with the fused spelling. The Gologorica registers carry a Maximilianus Antonius Josephus Defranceschi, born 9 January 1828, entered as mercator — a merchant.

people.heading: Four De Franceschi the collection is built on

rows.w: Politician and historian. Born in the house and died in it, eighty-four years apart.
Librarian and historian; Carlo's youngest child; author of the documented history of the County of Pazin.

Painter, and new to this archive. He illustrated Giuseppe Caprin's «Il Trecento a Trieste», and the copy in the family library carries Caprin's own hand: «A Giulio De Franceschi diligente ed amoroso illustratore di questo libro». His pencil drawings are in the archive boxes. He died at Gologorica in 1942 — the last of them in the house.
Lawyer and historian; Camillo's son. Three generations of historians from one house.

house.heading: What the house was
house.text: Seventeen of the twenty stamped bookplates in the collection belong to one man: Tomaso Luciani of Labin, 1818–1894, antiquarian, publicist and politician. And the reason his books are there is the reason the house matters — Luciani was a friend of Carlo's, and at Carlo's house in Gologorica he met the representatives of the Italian bourgeois, liberal and national opposition. The books are mostly seventeenth- and eighteenth-century; eight of them are Cicero.
house.then: The dedications point the same way. Books inscribed to Pietro Kandler, the father of Istrian historiography; to the archaeologist Alberto Puschi; to the politician Giorgio Pitacco; five of them to Andrea Amoroso of Rovinj. Among the authors doing the inscribing are the priest and polymath Petar Stanković of Barban and Attilio Hortis of Trieste. A farmhouse on a hill in the middle of Istria was on the circuit.

ask.heading: What to do about it
steps: Write to the Nacionalna i sveučilišna knjižnica u Zagrebu and ask for the box list of the De Franceschi family archive — the summary description of all fourteen boxes and seven folders already exists.
Ask specifically for the family correspondence and for the photograph album. This project has never seen a photograph of the Gologorica house.
Ask whether the estate documentation includes anything on the lease of the bishop of Pedena's «affitto fermo», which Carlo says his family held until the bishopric was suppressed.
Anita Marin of the NSK catalogued the collection and wrote the paper. She is the person who knows what is in those boxes.
And search the NSK catalogue for shelfmark PDF directly — 2,480 records are already public.
ask.drafted: The letter in the project repository at requests/nsk-de-franceschi-archive.md has been rewritten. The box list it was going to request turned out to be published already — so it now asks for the things a published inventory cannot give: images of specific items, and above all of the photograph album in box 6 and the Kandler correspondence in boxes 7 to 11.
ask.caution: One thing the letter says plainly, and this archive should too: no document yet links the Gračišće line this site follows to the Gologorica household of Carlo the historian. They are two families of one surname in two neighbouring parishes. The request is made as an interested descendant of the surname and the district, not as an heir — which is both truer and likelier to be well received.

source: Anita Marin, «Oznake vlasništva i posvete na knjigama Knjižnice obitelji De Franceschi» — Marks of ownership and dedications in the books of the De Franceschi family library — Libellarium 15 (2), 2024, pp. 25–46. Original scientific paper, open access, doi 10.15291/libellarium.4520. Published by the University of Zadar.

inventory.heading: The box list, published
inventory.lead: A second paper — Marin, Jurišić and Matijaca, «Arhiv obitelji De Franceschi u Nacionalnoj i sveučilišnoj knjižnici u Zagrebu», Arhivski vjesnik 67 (2024) — describes the archive box by box. It is open access. The shelfmark is PDF 2.337, and the arrangement is fourteen boxes and nine folders. What follows is what is in them.

boxes.w: Manuscript notes, drafts of historical research and sketches. Named manuscripts: «Memorie di Carlo De Franceschi», «Camillo De Franceschi 1887-89-92», «Versi giovanili di C. de F.». Letters, including one to the mayor of Trieste of 18 October 1901 signed «La Direzione della Biblioteca Civica — C. De Franceschi», and a folder «Corrispondenza» signed with Gian Pietro's initials. Letters came from Poreč, Pazin, Pula and Gologorica, and the family often wrote jointly — one of 27 June 1879 has Faustina on one side of the sheet and Camillo on the other. And then the domestic paper: the household accounts of Moncalvo — Gologorica — for 1925–26 and 1929–30, with bills for bricks, lime, cement, scissors, oil and alcohol; a notebook «Libro di famiglia Camillo De Franceschi» keeping accounts from 1900 to 1919; and a contract by which Giulio and Camillo let the second floor of the house to the parish priest Lodovico Zváček from 15 March to 15 May 1907.

Political and propaganda leaflets, society forms, cuttings from newspapers and books of the eighteenth to twentieth centuries, maps of Europe, Istria and «Il Veneto, le Alpi carniche e Giulie», and plans.

boxes.t: Transcripts, and a note on surnames
boxes.w: Drafts and transcripts by Carlo and Camillo — archival material on the French administration of Trieste, 1809–13; notes on the surnames of families of the Trieste district; material on the national composition of Istria; and material for the argument about the Istrian Razvod, which Carlo held to be a forgery. Also a manuscript by Friedrich von Grimschitz, the Austrian district governor who ran Istria from 1849 to 1861.

boxes.t: Camillo's working papers, and the family's verse
boxes.w: Camillo's drafts: the preface to the «Chartularium Piranese», «I primordi del movimento unitario a Trieste», «L'antico palazzo pretorio di Parenzo» — and his preface to his father's «Memorie». Beside them the family's own writing: «Poesie 1889» by Armella De Franceschi, Giulio's wife; Camillo's «Versi domestici italiani»; the student booklet of Carlo the younger from the University of Padua; a notebook of Italo's from 1921.

An album decorated with flowers and birds. Mostly postcards to Camillo, at his house in Trieste, at the Civica Biblioteca, and at the family estate at Gologorica — from Koper, Udine, Florence, Pula, Poreč, Portorož, Geneva, Venice, Paris, Rome and Bombay. Postcards to his wife Silvia. One from his son Italo in Rome. And one Camillo sent from Trieste on 20 March 1906 to his six-year-old son Carlo, who was staying with his uncle Giulio at Piran. Only eight photographs, on two pages. Separately, in a card envelope, the family photographs: several portraits of Carlo, a photograph of his bust at Pazin, signed school photographs from Trieste — and one woman, inscribed on the back «Maria De Franceschi, Parenzo, 187[?]».

boxes.t: The correspondence — five boxes of it
boxes.w: Private and business letters, kept in separate runs. Camillo's is the largest. Then Camillo's letters to his sister Faustina between 1886 and 1893; Vittorio's letters; and — the one this archive would open first — «Lettere archeologiche a Pietro Kandler», Carlo's long and rich correspondence with the Trieste historian. Among the other correspondents: Attilio Hortis, Ugo Inchiostri, Andrea Amoroso, Antonio Pogatschnig, Piero Pillepich, Francesco Salata, the philologists Matteo Bartoli of Labin and Giuseppe Vidossich of Koper, and Antonio Alisi.

Four envelopes of personalia, each titled: «Attestati e Documenti personali di Carlo De Franceschi da Moncalvo di Pisino storiografo istriano (1809-1893)»; «Documenti personali di Camillo de Franceschi»; «Attestati e documenti personale di Gian Pietro de Franceschi (1854-1884)»; and «Attestati e documenti personale di Giulio de Franceschi pittore accademico (1856-1942)». With them a rolled printed plan by the architect Giuseppe Hirsch — «Cappella della famiglia di Carlo de Franceschi nel cimitero di Moncalvo di Pisino», the family chapel in the cemetery at Gologorica — and a number of Giulio's pencil drawings.
Promotional material, blank postcards, reproductions of small pictures, cut-out illustrations and newspaper clippings.

folders.w: Thirty-six torn leaves of an older book printed in Italian and Latin side by side; a folded sheet with an embroidery pattern; two posters — the Italian Exposition of 1861 and the Trieste war exposition of 1917; five Lega Nazionale calendars for 1911, 1913, 1914, 1924 and 1925; and an older German one running from 22 September 1797 to 22 September 1799.
Thirty-four occasional pieces dedicated to Niccolò Tommaseo.

The household economy: records of income and expenditure, bills, Camillo's bank book and statements, and sale contracts — among them one of 1902 for a wood, signed by Giulio, Camillo and Faustina with Simon Rabar.

The unveiling of Carlo's bust at Pazin on 23 June 1929 — correspondence between the mayor of Pazin and Camillo, and photographs of the ceremony. With it: travel tickets, lottery slips, two postcards from Egypt to Camillo, a postcard bearing Hitler's picture (Olympia, 1936) addressed to Italo, and locks of hair in small envelopes marked 1887 and «G. O. D. F. 1884».

Death notices — Maria de Franceschi, Carlo de Franceschi, Gian Pietro de Franceschi, Elena Scampicchio, Carlo Combi — and press notices of deaths and memorials. Vittorio's letter to his cousin Camillo telling him of the death of their uncle Massimiliano. Wedding invitations. An older letter of 1789 with its seal. A list of Carlo's manuscript remains. And a kerchief with the flags of Trieste, Trento, Italy and Dalmatia.

A manuscript «Cose Istriane», dated 1850 and signed «Un Istriano»; manuscripts on parchment; poems by Silvio Benco and by Giuseppina Martinuzzi of Labin; and an occasional piece printed at Pola: «Nelle fauste occasioni delle nozze Maria De Franceschi — Luigi Salamon, Pola, 25 ottobre 1897».
Political and promotional material, incomplete parts of books, and cuttings.

inventory.span: The material runs from the eighteenth century to 1943, when the family moved to Rovinj and then settled permanently in Italy. Most of it is nineteenth- and early twentieth-century, and most of it is in Italian. The cataloguers note that nothing was thrown away — not a scrap of paper, not a note.

threads.heading: Three things in that list this archive should follow

rows.t: A De Franceschi married a Salamon
rows.w: Folder 6 holds a wedding piece printed at Pola: «Nelle fauste occasioni delle nozze Maria De Franceschi — Luigi Salamon, Pola, 25 ottobre 1897». This archive's own spine has Joannes Baptista Defranceschi of house 5, Gallignana, marrying Francisca Salomon in 1819. Salamon is a common enough Istrian name that this proves nothing — but it is the same pairing of surnames, seventy-eight years later, and nobody has looked at it.

Folder 5 has Vittorio writing to his cousin Camillo to tell him their uncle Massimiliano had died. The Gologorica parish registers give a Maximilianus Antonius Josephus Defranceschi, born 9 January 1828 and entered as mercator, a merchant; and one book in the library is signed «Massiliano Defranceschi». Three independent traces of one man.

Box 12 holds the architect's printed plan for «Cappella della famiglia di Carlo de Franceschi nel cimitero di Moncalvo di Pisino». There is a De Franceschi family chapel in the cemetery at Gologorica, and this archive has never recorded it, photographed it, or established whether it stands.
